To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Li-Fraumenii families are a unique resource for identifying individuals at high risk for specific cancers and for understanding the causes of those cancers.

Li-Fraumenie families have an increased cancer risk, that the risk is highest among those with a family history of Li-Fraumenii cancers, and that the excess cancer risk is greatest among those under age 45.

the Li-Fraumene cancer family syndrome is characterized by a high risk of breast cancer, sarcoma, brain tumors, and adrenocortical carcinoma in children and young and middle-aged adults and is likely to result from germ line mutations in the tumor suppresser gene p53.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the genetic epidemiology of breast cancer and the identification of genetic susceptibility to breast cancer in families.
the identification of genetic factors that influence susceptibility to cancer.
the identification of genetic risk factors in human populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Li-Fraumenii syndrome is a genetic cancer syndrome with a high probability that the underlying gene is p53.

the Li-Fraumene cancer family syndrome is a dominantly inherited cancer susceptibility syndrome that is characterized by an excess of cancers in childhood and adolescence, and that these tumors are most likely to occur in those at high genetic risk of carrying the syndrome gene.
